\begin{columns}
% =========================================================================================================== column 1
\column{0.25}
\block{Question and scope}{
Following NREL's Oregon offshore-wind study: \emph{how much new supply can the existing system host, and does the planned portfolio
need major grid improvements?}

\vspace{4mm}
Minas Gerais (MG), Brazil, net zero by 2050 (PLAC-MG). Network: the MG main grid of the EPE 2035 planning case, \Nmonlines{} lines $\ge$230~kV and \Nmontx{} transformer branches
monitored, \Nncont{} \mbox{N-1} contingencies. A facility is attributed to the portfolio inside the CAISO 5\% circle (distribution factor
$\ge$5\% or flow impact $\ge$5\% of its rating).
}

\centering
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%

\block{Resource adequacy}{
\centering
\tab{\begin{tabular}{llrr}
\toprule
Year & Method, case & \shortstack[r]{EUE\\(GWh) \dn} & \shortstack[r]{Firm gap\\(MW) \dn} \\
\midrule
2035 & COPT (capacity only) & -- & surplus \NpcsurplusA \\
2035 & Monte Carlo, normal & \NeueAnormalname & \NgapAnormalname \\
2035 & Monte Carlo, dry & \NeueAdryname & \NgapAdryname \\
2050 & COPT (capacity only) & -- & surplus \NpcsurplusB \\
2050 & Monte Carlo, normal & \NeueBnormalname & $\le$\NgapBnormalname \\
2050 & Monte Carlo, dry & \NeueBdryname & $\le$\NgapBdryname \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\vspace{2mm}\raggedright\legend

\vspace{4mm}
Method A: capacity outage probability table with NERC GADS EFORd by unit class. Method B: sequential Monte Carlo with two-state
outage histories, each an 8,760-hour energy-limited PyPSA dispatch (monthly hydro budgets, storage); firm gaps by bisection
(resolution \Ngapres~MW). \textbf{2050 is energy-limited, not capacity-limited:} the COPT finds a surplus, while the energy-limited
dispatch falls short in every simulated year.
}

\quad without small line needs & \NgroupsexclR & \NcapexexclR & \NbcrRexcl \\
Batteries at load buses & \NgroupsL & \NcapexL & \NbcrL \\

\vspace{2mm}\raggedright\legend

\vspace{4mm}
Alternatives per attributable group follow the PG\&E cluster-study structure, costed from EPE/ANEEL unit costs, and the plan is verified

revenue requirement; at VOLL $-$50\% the full plan keeps BCR \NbcrRmin. Moving the batteries to load buses alone saves
\RS\Nbenreloc~M/yr.
}

\raggedright
\textbf{P7 (existing parallel circuits assumed to share towers):} \Npremn{} more 230~kV circuits, \RS\Npremcapex~M; full-plan BCR
\Nprembcr.

\vspace{3mm}
\textbf{AC voltage, N-0:} new out-of-limit buses: \NacnewhighA{} high (2035), \NacnewlowB{} low (2050 reference siting), up to
\NacnewhighBL{} high with batteries at load (reactive switching not modelled).

\vspace{3mm}
\textbf{Annual vs hourly matching (2050):} annual matching lowers cost by \NmatchabsAone\% if \NmatchAexports~TWh of exports can be
delivered.

\vspace{3mm}
\textbf{Limits:} one evening network snapshot and one weather year; the 2050 network is the 2035 topology; DC flows.
}

\block{Findings}{
\raggedright
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{2035 needs no major grid improvement:} $\alpha$ = \NalphaASthreeeveningnonsolar--\NalphaASonepeakdelivery, no
congestion cost, adequate.
\item \textbf{2050 midday solar is deliverable} ($\alpha$ = \NalphaBSonepeakdelivery); \textbf{evening battery discharge is not}
($\alpha$ = \NalphaBSthreeeveningnonsolar--\NalphaBHSNcaiso).
\item \textbf{Battery siting is the cheapest fix:} one bank (\RS\NcapexL~M) at load buses.
\item \textbf{With northern batteries the plan is justified:} \NgroupsR{} groups, \RS\NcapexexclR--\NcapexR~M, BCR
\NbcrRfull--\NbcrRexcl.
\item \textbf{2050 adequacy is limited by hydro energy, not capacity:} up to \NgapBnormalname~MW (normal) and \NgapBdryname~MW
(dry) of firm capacity.
\item \textbf{Curtailment comes from the hourly local-balance rule:} \Nunusedbcopperplate~TWh (\Nunusedpctbcopperplate\%) unused even
without network limits; congestion adds \Ncongcurtpctbexistinggrid\%, below the 5\% screen.
\item \textbf{The definition of fossil-free matters:} annual matching costs \NmatchabsAone\% less.
\end{enumerate}
}
